validated_results.title: Toenail selenium concentrations and bladder cancer risk in women and men.
validated_results.reason: This prospective nested case-control study evaluated prediagnostic toenail selenium concentrations and incident bladder cancer risk in men and women.

cases.excerpt: From the time of the toenail collection through 2000, 338 incident cases with toenail samples were available for the selenium analyses (222 men; 116 women).

design.excerpt: in a nested case–control study of 338 cases and 341 matched controls.

timing.excerpt: Participants with bladder cancer were eligible for this analysis if the cancer diagnosis occurred after the toenail samples were obtained

continent.excerpt: Selenium concentrations were measured in two batches by Dr Morris at the University of Missouri Research Reactor, Columbia, MO, USA

ethnicity.excerpt: The Health Professionals Follow-Up Study (HPFS) and the Nurses' Health Study (NHS) cohorts provided data for our analyses

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Selenium concentrations were measured in two batches by Dr Morris at the University of Missouri Research Reactor, Columbia, MO, USA, using neutron activation analysis (NAA)

p_value.excerpt: In a conditional regression model, higher toenail selenium concentrations were associated with significantly lower risk of bladder cancer in women ( P for trend=0.02), but not in men ( Table 2 ).
